  "reasons": [
    "Money received from a shareholder towards an uncalled instalment represents calls in advance.",
    "Under NCERT accounting principles, calls received in advance are credited to Calls in Advance Account and treated as a liability until adjusted on the due date."
  ],
  "syllabus_chapter": "Share Capital",

    },
    {
      "option": "D",

    {

      "premise_source": "excerpt",
      "evidence_id": "E1.1",
      "premise_quote": "The amount received in advance is a liability of the company and should be credited to ‘Call in Advance Account.”",
      "reason": "It must be credited to Calls in Advance Account as a liability, not to Share Capital Account."
    },
    {
      "option": "B",
      "status": "contradicted",
      "false_part": "Credit it to Calls in Arrears A/c and show it as an asset of the company",
      "premise_source": "excerpt",
      "evidence_id": "E1.1",
      "premise_quote": "The amount received in advance is a liability of the company and should be credited to ‘Call in Advance Account.”",
      "reason": "The call is not yet made, so it is Calls in Advance and not Calls in Arrears."
